This year, Russian and Ukrainian drones have repeatedly breached the airspace and territorial waters of Romania, officials in the European Union and ‌NATO member state ⁠neighbouring Ukraine have said. "Last night, the LPG Gas Lisbon, a Liberian-flagged vessel, was ⁠hit outside Romanian territorial waters, approximately 20 nautical miles (40 km) off the Romanian coast," Dan wrote ​on X. Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha greeted the delegations, which included Estonian PM Kristen Michal, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Latvian PM Andris Kulbergs, Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre, and Danish PM Mette Frederiksen. by Kyiv Post | Aug. 23, 2026, 1:03 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha and Finnish President Alexander Stubb arrive in Kyiv on Aug. 23. (Photo: Andriy Sybiha/X) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Leaders from six European nations arrived in Kyiv on the morning of Sunday, Aug. 23, to participate in commemorations for Ukraine’s Flag Day and Independence Day, as well as a series of high-level diplomatic meetings. Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andri Sybiha announced that he greeted the leaders of Denmark , Estonia , Finland , Latvia , Lithuania , and Norway at the Kyiv railway station. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “On the eve of Independence Day, we feel that we are not alone. Our allies are by our side,” Sybiha wrote on X. “They will hold bilateral and multilateral talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky . Important decisions will be made and important statements will be issued.” Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal also confirmed his arrival on X, noting the shared history of Estonia and Ukraine restoring their independence 35 years ago. Advertisement “[Russian President Vladimir] Putin hopes that time is on his side. Our task is to prove him wrong,” Michal wrote. “Ukraine must have everything necessary to defend itself and decide its future independently.” Finnish President Alexander Stubb arrived for a two-day visit accompanied by his wife, Suzanne Innes-Stubb, according to the Finnish broadcaster YLE . The Finnish delegation also includes the Commander of the Defense Forces, Janne Jaakkola, and a group of entrepreneurs. Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs is also among the visiting delegation. According to the Baltic news outlet BB.lv , Kulbergs emphasized Latvia’s determination to help Ukraine prepare for the upcoming winter. Before arriving in the capital, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre condemned the recent wave of Russian strikes across Ukraine. “Russia has no remorse when it comes to distinguishing between civilian and military targets,” Støre stated. “It is precisely civilian infrastructure, residential buildings, schools, and hospitals that have suffered, which is a systematic violation of international law.” Advertisement Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen also commented on the recent Russian attacks, emphasizing the necessity of continued support for Ukraine. Ahead of our Independence Day, we feel we are not alone. Our allies are with us. Today in the morning, I was pleased to welcome leaders of Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, alongside other high representatives, at the Kyiv Railway Station. They will hold… pic.twitter.com/NmPgIVH1g3 — Andrii Sybiha 🇺🇦 (@andrii_sybiha) August 23, 2026 Diplomatic summits and allied support The visiting leaders are scheduled to participate in a series of events over the next two days, including the national holiday commemorations and bilateral meetings with President Zelensky. The officials will also take part in a summit of the NB8 (Nordic-Baltic Eight) format, which brings together the five Nordic and three Baltic states. Additionally, the leaders are expected to attend a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, a group coordinating international support for Ukraine, which is scheduled to convene in Kyiv on Monday, Aug. 24. The arrival of the Nordic and Baltic leaders follows the earlier arrival of Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda , who announced on Sunday morning that he would also be participating in the NB8 discussions and the Coalition of the Willing meeting. https://www.dw.com/en/elon-musk-ordered-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OUWh Ukraine has accused Elon Musk's SpaceX of restricting Starlink service in the country [FILE: May 30, 2025] Image: Nathan Howard/REUTERS Advertisement Tech billionaire Elon Musk ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on , the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing US officials. Kyiv uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations . Restricting the service means restricting the country's attack and defense missions against Russia. Last week, Musk capped the speeds at which Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network, the report said, citing unnamed sources. The move rendered some offensive drones and interceptor drones virtually useless, it added. Two people told the Journal that Musk and US President Donald Trump discussed the Starlink decision in a call soon after the slowdown became public. Some US officials, the report said, believed Musk acted unilaterally and that Trump did not specifically order retribution against Ukraine. However, one person familiar with the situation said Musk spoke with multiple senior administration officials, including Trump, before imposing the speed cap. Both Musk and Trump have expressed anger at Ukraine for attacking Russian diesel refineries in recent weeks , which the president blames for high energy prices. The report also comes after Trump's comments last week that he did not think either he or Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access. Musk had said that any limits on speed or use were decided by the US military or the president. Musk, SpaceX, and the White House are yet to respond to the report. US envoy Steve Witkoff is set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday after what a US official called "constructive" talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway , as Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war . https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria-how-the-pc.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PRq5 Prefer DW on Google Nigeria's 2027 elections take place against the backdrop of AI-driven disinformation Image: Adekunle Ajayi/NurPhoto/picture alliance Advertisement Nigeria has just over two months to go to the polls, with incumbent President Bola Tinubu running on a ticket focused on combating raging insecurity and resolving the nation's economic crisis . He faces off against former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and senior opposition figure Peter Obi. The country's electoral body, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), recently released its preliminary voter's register, which reportedly is riddled with images believed to have been generated using artificial intelligence (AI) . Among the telltale signs of AI usage were exaggerated facial features in images, and inconsistencies on the electoral registers, such as duplicates of names and even identities of people who since the previous election had died. The development raises concerns about the body's overall preparedness ahead of the country's upcoming 2027 general elections; instead of making the upcoming vote more transparent by allowing access to its procedures, INEC has come under fire amid broader controversies about the expanding influence of AI in elections across the continent. Is Nigeria becoming a one-party state? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Fake news: Nothing new in Nigeria Joash Amupitan, the chairman of the commission, said the body is now investigating the development, focusing on discrepancies potentially created by AI-use. To this end, he announced the establishment of a dedicated unit to monitor AI-related threats, detect deepfakes and strengthen the integrity of the electoral process, warning that the credibility of the upcoming elections could otherwise be under attack. However, even prior to the proliferation of AI across Africa and indeed the globe, this would not be the first time that Nigeria finds itself in the unfortunate position of having to deal with the circulation of fabricated images , doctored audio and fake videos online; in the run up to the 2023 elections , deepfakes falsely linking candidates to terror-related activities filled social media platforms. These are often designed to promote certain candidates, or to discredit opponents in a bid to influence public perception, which now with the use of AI could create disinformation campaigns of new proportions. Supporters of a particular candidate in the election can be manipulated easily to believe AI-driven fake news Image: Sani Maikatanga/AP Photo/picture alliance Artificial Intelligence: Various effects on voter behavior Lois Ugbede, the assistant editor at the factchecking platform DUBAWA, told DW that "based on our monitoring so far, AI-driven disinformation is serious and is becoming commonplace." "This could influence political discourse and voter behavior ahead of 2027 because we are already seeing parties using inflated crowds to show that they have a large followership or support," she added. At the same time, rather than influencing the vote in favor of any particular candidate, "the deeper danger is that people may begin to doubt authentic information simply because they know convincing AI generated fakes are possible," says Akintunde Babatunde, Executive Director of the Abuja-based Center for Journalism, Innovation and Development (CJID)." "We often focus on the risk of people believing an AI-generated falsehood, but there is another problem where genuine evidence can be dismissed as AI generated," he noted, citing instances of a lawmaker who recently made inflammatory remarks during a campaign rally — but then claimed the clips were manipulated. Have some elections become an empty ritual? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Further pitfalls behind a lack of safeguards against AI Chibuike Mgbeahuruike, an election consultant at the Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD-West Africa), meanwhile told DW that apart from the spread of synthetic content online, AI intrusion into INEC's portal could also "undermine its institutional credibility, especially with the low level of confidence that we are already witnessing." He added however that AI itself is not inherently a threat to electoral integrity, but that the real threat rather lies in "the absence of effective accountability for its deployment," as innovations in tech increasingly appear to infiltrate governments and their democratic processes. "Voters must have confidence … that the technology is also transparent, accountable and independently scrutinized, and ultimately subject to human and institutional oversight," Mgbeahuruike said. Journalists can be just as susceptible to disinformation created by AI and other technologies Image: Emmanuel Osodi/AA/picture alliance The Director-General of Voice of Nigeria (VON), Mallam Jibrin Baba Ndace, agrees, urging journalists at a recent conference also to not fall into the trap of believing reports, which later could turn out to be false due to AI manipulation. He stressed the importance of protection measures and due diligence in news media, with the growing inability of public institutions like INEC to provide impartial information due to the use and influence of AI and other election-related tech. Nigeria's marred relationship with new tech in elections Beyond AI, Nigeria's electoral processes have undergone various technological shifts over the years in hopes of improving transparency while increasing efficiency. Electoral authorities first deployed electronic assistance in 2011, when Direct Data Capture Machines were introduced; the devices collect voters' biometrics by scanning fingerprints or capturing facial recognition data with webcams to stop voters from submitting multiple ballots. Ten years later, a new system called the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) was introduced as the new standard, designed to combine fingerprints with facial recognition; however, during the 2023 general elections, this voting process was marred by system failures of BVAS, as poor cell signal delayed these voter accreditation procedures. In Nigeria, voting procedures have increasingly been digitalized since 2011 Image: Pius Utomi Ekpei/AFP However, with INEC tallying more than 103 million Nigerians registered to participate in the coming poll, disinformation, fake news and technological challenges amount to only few of several concerns pertaining to Nigeria's democracy: Voter apathy has become a particular concern, especially among the country's youth; the 2023 elections recorded the lowest voter turnout since the country's return to democratic rule in 1999, with merely 27 percent of registered voters going to the polls.
